deep.reconstruction:
The page is a numerical conversion (look-up) table, not a derivation. It has two blocks. The left block covers arguments n = 575 to 600 and the right block covers n = 600 to 625. Next to each n is an angle in degrees, minutes and seconds, and a third column gives first differences in arcseconds.

All entries are reproduced exactly (to 0.1") by one linear formula:
A(n) = 17°17'50.0" + 21.84" · (n − 600).
- A(575) = 17°8'44.0".
- A(625) = 17°26'56.0".
- The total change over 50 units is 18'12" = 1092", so the step is 21.84" per unit.

The tabulated values are the exact linear values rounded to 0.1". Examples: 9'5.84" is written 9'5.8"; 10'11.36" is written 10'11.4"; 12'0.56" is written 12'0.6"; 21'6.56" is written 21'6.6". So the writer most likely built the table by repeatedly adding 21.84", then rounding.

The difference column (21.8 / 21.9) is just the differences of the rounded entries. Because 5 × 21.84" = 109.2" exactly, the differences repeat with period 5: 21.8, 21.9, 21.8, 21.9, 21.8.

Interpretation (mine, plausible but not certain): this is a table converting scale readings of a declination magnetometer (mirror-and-scale reading, with a constant angular value of 21.84" per scale division) into absolute magnetic declination near 17°.
- About 17° is a plausible Göttingen west declination around 1850.
- The previous page mentions Dase and Clausen's computations of π, which also fits a date in the late 1840s or 1850s.
- If the scale divisions are millimetres, 21.84" per division corresponds to a mirror-to-scale distance of about 206265/(2 · 21.84) ≈ 4722 mm. This assumes the doubling of the reflected angle and ignores any torsion correction.

Nothing deeper is computed on the page.
errors: No computational errors found: every entry agrees with 17°17'50" + 21.84"(n−600) rounded to 0.1".

In the left difference column, the transcription gives 21.9 for the step 582→583 (11'16.9" → 11'38.7"), but the actual difference is 21.8. The parallel right-hand step (607→608) is correctly 21.8. This is either a slip in the manuscript or a misreading of the image.

results.what: Linear conversion table A(n) = 17°17'50" + 21.84"·(n−600) for n = 575..625, built by repeated addition with rounding and a difference check column
results.modern_name: Linear calibration / look-up table (scale reading to angle, presumably magnetometer declination)
results.usually_credited_to: Routine observational practice; the mirror-scale magnetometer method is due to Gauss (1832–1834) and Gauss–Weber

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine arithmetic conversion table of the kind produced in magnetic-observatory work. It contains no mathematical content beyond linear interpolation and difference checking.

checkable.asserts: The 575→600 block is consistent with the same step of 21.84".
This reproduces the seconds part of every tabulated value (e.g. 5.8, 27.7, 49.5, 11.4, ...), with minutes = floor(total/60) relative to 17°.
Five steps sum to 109.2" exactly, which explains the period-5 pattern 21.8, 21.9, 21.8, 21.9, 21.8 in the differences.
The difference between 11'16.9" and 11'38.7" is 21.8, not 21.9 as transcribed.

transcription_corrections: Each difference value sits between two rows and belongs to the interval (n−1 → n). The transcription attaches it to the lower row, which is acceptable but should be read that way.
The difference recorded for 582→583 in the left block should be 21,8 by computation; the transcription has 21,9. Re-check the image.
The left block's header value should read 17° 8' 44,0" (degree sign omitted in the manuscript); the angles are in degrees, minutes and seconds throughout.
The struck-out header text '155 nf 19' is probably an archival or shelf mark, not mathematical content.
